what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the tools in tools/where-a-person-stands: what each tool does, what it takes and gives back, how it runs, and the stance record it keeps.

payload.label: Keep where you stand on something
payload.job: Write down whether a person agrees, disagrees or partly agrees with something made for them, such as a title, a take, a plan or a file, in their own words
payload.description: Give kind (what the thing is: a title, a take, a plan, a file), the thing (artifact_ref, its identity: 1f: and 64 hex digits, or file: and that identity; or the thing itself: text, contains for a part of a text, or view for any JSON, with fold, how its owner says two texts are the same), stance (agree, disagree or partly, or null to take a stand back), why (the person's own words, kept exactly) and answered_by "person": only send what the person said. Returns the stance record, kept in the person's records as one record per kind and identity (stance:<kind>:<identity>), so a change of mind is a new version and every earlier stand stays in its history. Text is identified folded, so the same title typed again finds the same stand. A name instead of an identity, or a stand not answered by the person, is refused.

kind.description: What kind of thing the stand is on (title, voice take, plan, file)

artifact_ref.description: The identity of the thing the stand is on

text.description: The thing itself, when it is a text

contains.description: A part of a text the person named

view.description: The thing itself, when it is JSON (a plan, a measure report)

fold.description: How two texts are the same text, as the owner of the rules declares it: lowercase, quotes ([[from characters, to]]), collapse_space, strip_trailing (a pattern)

stance.description: Where the person stands; null takes the stand back

why.description: The person's own words, exactly as they said them

answered_by.description: Always person: a stand is only ever theirs

by.description: Who sent it (the app or chat), when it is not the person's own screen

at.description: When they said it, as an ISO time (default: now)

rule.description: One rule of the person's that this stand names: an agree on an exact text then waives that rule on that text alone. Its own record.

source_text.description: The whole text of the file the words were said in (a chat export, a transcript, a note). Given, why must appear in it literally, or nothing is kept, and the record names where (said_from).

source.description: The name of that file; a name ending .jsonl is read as JSON lines, where words are kept escaped

after_line.description: The words must be at or after this line of source_text (default 1)

provenance.source: the record-stance owner of the decision engine, as a tool: the stand is a record, its history is the record's versions

record_model._what: The record kinds, indexes and links this tool keeps (moved unchanged from trillion-rust's one record model: src/record_model_policy/record-model.json, src/record_indexes/record-indexes.json, product/lists.json field_kinds and product/record-sharing.json links).

kinds._read_by: src/record-stance.mjs: the person's stand, its history and durable correction recovery
src/private-responses.mjs: the person's own reactions on one record or part of it

record_model._what_moved: Moved here from tools/keep-a-record-library-valid, where they were held unchanged after the engine's one record model left it (old trillion src/record-model.json and src/record-indexes.json): the kinds this tool's job keeps, each as old trillion declared it.

payload.label: Read where you stand on things
payload.job: See whether a person agrees, disagrees or partly agrees with one thing made for them, in their own words, with every time they changed their mind
payload.description: Two steps. First page records:history at @own-records for the thing's stance record (id stance:<kind>:<identity>, limit up to 100, before_version from next) until next is null; this tool cannot read the person's records itself. Then give the versions of every page together and next from the last page, exactly as records:history returns them. Returns stand: its stand now (the newest version), said, why in the person's own words, by, at, version, earlier (every version before it, oldest first, a tombstone as deleted) and complete (false while next is not null: earlier stands not yet read are unknown); and choices, the stands a person can take. No version, a tombstone or a stand taken back reads stance null with taken_back: silence is not agreement.

value.description: The stance record at that version; null for a tombstone

deleted.description: True for a tombstone: the record was removed at that version

versions.description: The versions records:history returned, from every page read, in any order

next.description: next from the last page read; null when the oldest version was read

provenance.source: the record-stance owner of the decision engine, as a tool: the stand is a record, its history is the record's versions

payload.label: Plan moving kept stands into stance records
payload.job: Turn stands a person took that were kept somewhere else into their stance records, with every earlier stand as an earlier version, and show what would change before anything is written
payload.description: Give stances (rows: kind, text, contains or view, stance, why, by, at, earlier as [{stance, why, at}], and the old ref if there was one) and fold, how the owner of the rules says two texts are the same. Returns writes, the record versions to send one at a time in order (each record's earlier stands first, oldest first), and summary: rows, records and versions by kind, refs_changed (rows whose identity differs from their old ref) collisions (records two or more rows became under the fold, with each row's text and time), already (versions in kept, not written again) and unverified (rows whose words are not in their source, never written). A row may name a rule (a waiver stand) and a source with after_line, and so may each of its earlier stands; every stand naming a source is checked against sources, and a row any of whose words are not there is listed in unverified by the id of the record it would have been. summary_only true leaves the writes out. It writes nothing.

stances.description: The stands kept elsewhere, one row per thing; a row and each of its earlier stands may name the source its words were said in (source, after_line)

fold.description: How two texts are the same text, as the owner of the rules declares it: lowercase, quotes ([[from characters, to]]), collapse_space, strip_trailing (a pattern)

by.description: Who a row with no by was said through (default person)

sources.description: The whole text of each source a row names in its source field: { <name>: <text> }. A row whose why is not literally in its source (at or after its after_line) is listed in summary.unverified and not written.

kept.description: Versions an earlier run already wrote ({ id, stance, why, at }); the same version is not written again and is counted in summary.already

provenance.source: the record-stance owner of the decision engine, as a tool: the stand is a record, its history is the record's versions

payload.label: Keep rulings on lines
payload.job: Write down rulings on single lines of copy, such as a line a checker flagged for the person or a reviewer's good or bad, as rows of the person's Checks list
payload.description: Give rows (each ruling: text, verdict, by, and optionally rule, kind, at, where and any other field kept), existing (the rulings already in list:checks, as records:list type record:check prefix record:check:ruling- pages them, so a ruling is written once) and settings_record (the person's row of list:settings for this tool as records:read gives it: unruled_part_of, the check branch a ruling with no rule goes under; refuse, [{ field, one_of: [values] } or { field, contains_one_of: [path parts] }] such as a test piece or a temporary folder; place, { field, pattern } that reads a ruling's place from its where; hand_rulings, the words a ruling given by hand may use; escalated_verdicts), or those fields themselves. by_hand true checks hand_rulings. Returns write, the records:write input to send at @own-records: one record:check per text, verdict, by and rule (id record:check:ruling-<BLAKE3 hex>, kind labelled-line, or escalated-line for an escalated line, part_of its rule or unruled_part_of, its copy kind as line_kind), and fresh, how many are new. A write holding a refused row is refused whole. It writes nothing.

rows.description: Rulings on single lines: text, verdict (bad, good, escalated or any one word), by (who gave it), rule (optional), at (optional) and any other field the list keeps (where, kind, p_fail, why, note)

at.description: When, for a ruling without its own at (default now)

settings_record.description: The person's row of list:settings for this tool (record:setting:where-a-person-stands~<scope kind>~<scope id>) as records:read gives it, its value, or a list of them; read by tools/settings. The input's own fields win over it

existing.description: The rulings already in the list (records or their values)

refuse.description: The list's refuse setting: [{ field, one_of?: [values], contains_one_of?: [path parts] }]

place.description: { field, pattern }: the field a ruling's place is kept in and the pattern whose first group reads it from where

by_hand.description: The rows were given by hand: each field must use a word hand_rulings allows

hand_rulings.description: { field: [words] } a ruling given by hand may use

unruled_part_of.description: The check branch a ruling that names no rule is kept under (the person's setting, such as content-production)

escalated_verdicts.description: The verdict words that mark a line a checker escalated (default [escalated]): kept as kind escalated-line

provenance.source: the copy gate's verdict log of the decision engine's launch film work (verdicts.mjs), as a tool: a ruling is a row of the person's list, one record per text, verdict, by and rule

payload.label: Make examples from rulings on lines
payload.job: Make labelled examples for calibrating a small model from the rulings a person gave on lines of copy, and from lines they said themselves
payload.description: Give rulings (the person's ruling rows of list:checks, records:list type record:check prefix record:check:ruling-, as records or values), real (who counts), needs (fields a ruling must carry to count), and optionally speech (lines they said, each with sets), speech_set, exclude (lists of lines a model was trained on), bad_label (the label a bad example carries in bad_for), contexts ({ text: context }) and verdicts ({ bad, good }). Returns items ({ text, good, bad_for, split, source: ruling or speech, context }) and left_out (texts ruled both ways, texts in exclude). Only rulings by the people in real count. Any of these may come from settings_record, the person's setting for this tool (their row of list:settings as records:read gives it, read by tools/settings); the input's own fields win. It writes nothing.

rulings.description: Rulings on single lines: text, verdict (bad, good, escalated or any one word), by (who gave it), rule (optional), at (optional) and any other field the list keeps (where, kind, p_fail, why, note)

real.description: Who counts as real: the people whose rulings count (a ruling by anyone else is never an example)

needs.description: Fields a ruling must carry to count, such as the piece it was judged in

speech.description: Lines the person said, each { text, sets }

exclude.description: Lists of lines (texts or { text }) a model was trained on; never examples

verdicts.description: The two verdict words: { bad, good } (default bad and good)

settings_record.description: The person's row of list:settings for this tool (record:setting:where-a-person-stands~<scope kind>~<scope id>) as records:read gives it, its value, or a list of them; read by tools/settings. The input's own fields win over it

provenance.source: the copy gate's verdict log of the decision engine's launch film work (verdicts.mjs), as a tool: a ruling is a row of the person's list, one record per text, verdict, by and rule

payload.label: Make examples from the options a person picked
payload.job: Make labelled examples for calibrating a small model from which options of a piece a person picked or rejected, and the lines they named
payload.description: Give films (each piece: name, gate (its pick settings: picked_verdicts and pick_labels with spec_globs using {option}, and optionally words, exclude, rejected_lines, text_keys, spoken_lead_s), decisions (its pick rows: option_id, verdict, lines, reason_verbatim; the last row of an option governs), files (the piece's file paths) and units ({ <spec path>: [{ text, kind, context }] }, the lines of each spec read so far)), and optionally rulings with real and needs (a text ruled directly is left out: the ruling wins), bad_label and rejected (the pattern a rejecting verdict matches, default ^rejected). Units of a picked option are good except the lines its row names; a rejection labels bad only the lines it names. Returns items, left_out (excluded, ruled_directly, both_labels, no_spec, several_specs) and units_needed: the specs whose lines to read and send again. Any of these may come from settings_record, the person's setting for this tool (their row of list:settings as records:read gives it, read by tools/settings); the input's own fields win. It writes nothing.

films.description: The pieces: { name, gate, decisions, files, units }

rulings.description: Rulings on single lines: text, verdict (bad, good, escalated or any one word), by (who gave it), rule (optional), at (optional) and any other field the list keeps (where, kind, p_fail, why, note)

real.description: Who counts as real: the people whose rulings count (a ruling by anyone else is never an example)

needs.description: Fields a ruling must carry to count, such as the piece it was judged in

verdicts.description: The two verdict words: { bad, good } (default bad and good)

payload.label: Count the real bad rulings on lines
payload.job: Count how many lines a person ruled bad, whether that is enough to let a model row fail lines, and how many of them each model row catches
payload.description: Give rulings (the person's ruling rows of list:checks, records:list type record:check prefix record:check:ruling-, as records or values) and settings_record (the person's setting for this tool: real, who counts; needs, fields a ruling must carry to count; needed, how many real bad rulings a model row needs before it may fail lines; and optionally verdict, the bad word, and default_kind), or those fields themselves. Returns real_bad_film (the real bad rulings), needed, promotion_allowed, counts (every "<by> <verdict>" of the log) and bad_lines (one per text: text, kind, where), the lines to check. Send again with rules (the model rows, [{ id, ask: { calibration: { t_fail } } }]) and results (the check's results on the bad lines: [{ text, uncertain: [{ rule, p_fail }] }]) to add escalated_by_any, per_rule (lines each row catches at its own t_fail) and unanswered. It runs no check and writes nothing.

rulings.description: Rulings on single lines: text, verdict (bad, good, escalated or any one word), by (who gave it), rule (optional), at (optional) and any other field the list keeps (where, kind, p_fail, why, note)

real.description: Who counts as real: the people whose rulings count (a ruling by anyone else is never an example)

needs.description: Fields a ruling must carry to count, such as the piece it was judged in

rules.description: The model rows: [{ id, ask: { calibration: { t_fail } } }] as the person's check rows keep them

results.description: The check's results on bad_lines: [{ text, uncertain: [{ rule, p_fail }] }]

payload.label: Count where a person stands
payload.job: Count the stands a person has taken, by kind of thing and by stand, with how many changed their mind and how many took a stand back
payload.description: Give stands: the stands read back (each the answer of tool:read-where-you-stand, or a stance record's value: kind, stance, and earlier when its history was read). Returns read (how many), by_kind ({ kind: { stance: count } }), with_history (stands with earlier stands) and taken_back (read with no stand now). It reads and writes nothing.

stands.description: The stands read back: standFrom answers or stance record values
